title: «Las cinco semillas de naranja», The Strand Magazine, noviembre de 1891

catalog.label: «Las cinco semillas de naranja», The Strand Magazine, vol. II (noviembre de 1891)

parts.text: Aventuras de Sherlock Holmes V\. — Las cinco semillas de naranja {{#ano_87 q:ano_87|[[ano_87|El año 87]] nos trajo una larga serie de casos de mayor o menor interés, de los que conservo las notas.}} {{#equinoccio q:equinoccio|Era a fines de septiembre, y los vendavales del equinoccio se habían desatado con una violencia excepcional.}} {{#fichero q:fichero|[[holmes|Sherlock Holmes]], malhumorado, ordenaba con referencias cruzadas sus archivos del crimen a un lado de la chimenea, mientras yo, al otro, me hundía en una de las espléndidas novelas marineras de [[clark_russell|Clark Russell]].}} {{#madre a:inc07 q:madre|[[esposa|Mi mujer]] había ido a visitar a [[madre_de_mary|su madre]], y por unos días volvía yo a habitar mis viejas habitaciones de [[baker_street|Baker Street]].}} Aquella noche sonó la campanilla. El visitante era joven, de veintidós años a lo sumo, bien arreglado y pulcramente vestido. —He oído hablar de usted, señor Holmes. {{#prendergast e:john_openshaw q:prendergast|El mayor Prendergast me contó cómo lo salvó en el escándalo del [[tankerville|club Tankerville]].}} —Ah, sí. Lo acusaron injustamente de hacer trampas a las cartas. —Dijo que usted podía resolverlo todo. —Dijo demasiado. —Que a usted nunca lo han vencido. {{#una_mujer a:inc08 e:holmes e:ano_87 q:una_mujer|—Me han vencido cuatro veces: tres, unos hombres, y una, una mujer.}}

src_en.ano_87: The year ’87 furnished us with a long series of cases of greater or less interest, of which I retain the records.
src_en.equinoccio: It was in the latter days of September, and the equinoctial gales had set in with exceptional violence.
src_en.fichero: Sherlock Holmes sat moodily at one side of the fireplace cross-indexing his records of crime, while I at the other was deep in one of Clark Russell’s fine sea-stories
src_en.madre: My wife was on a visit to her mother’s, and for a few days I was a dweller once more in my old quarters at Baker Street.
src_en.prendergast: I heard from Major Prendergast how you saved him in the Tankerville Club scandal.
src_en.una_mujer: I have been beaten four times—three times by men, and once by a woman.
src_en.marzo_1883: One day—it was in March, 1883—a letter with a foreign stamp lay upon the table in front of the colonel’s plate.
src_en.sin_amigos: It was not a common thing for him to receive letters, for his bills were all paid in ready money, and he had no friends of any sort.
src_en.pepitas: Opening it hurriedly, out there jumped five little dried orange pips, which pattered down upon his plate.
src_en.kkk: ‘K. K. K.!’ he shrieked, and then, ‘My God, my God, my sins have overtaken me!’
src_en.sobre: The young man took from his waistcoat a crumpled envelope, and turning to the table he shook out upon it five little dried orange pips.
